newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold still faces test of lows.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold still faces test of lows.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold is trying to hold on to the flimsy $340 level but is more likely to lose its foothold and slide towards this year's low of $336.15, analysts said on Thursday.
Silver's upside was limited to $4.72 and it too faced a grim prospect despite Wednesday's gains. Platinum is treading a range.

GOLD - U.S. first quarter GDP data pointing to an inflation pick-up kicked gold out of it's lethargic mood on Wednesday, but only briefly as prices settled back below $340.00 after rallying to $341.25.
Sentiment remained overwhelmingly bearish and most analysts expected a test of support at the February 12 low of $336.15 at some stage in the near term.
This might not happen on Thursday though, as most of Europe is closed for May Day holidays.
"We had some gains yesterday but we lost them very quickly," said precious metals dealer Morris Emmanuel at Swiss-based Socofinance.
"For the time being we are stuck in the $336-$341 range," he added.
If a downtrend line extending from the March high of $363.95 continued to hold, gold's upside would be capped at $340.00, chartists said.
"Initially place (support) at $338.50, which if breached would suggest a target of $330," said analyst Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff.
On the upside, resistance was to be heavily felt at $342.50 but in the unlikely event of a rally beyond this point, gold would be faced with the rock-solid barrier of $345.00, chartists said.
